claims.text: The rider's foundational burden is satisfied on the face of the bundle, so nothing turns on identification: the trip record (EV-TRIP-00102), the GPS trace (EV-GPS-00102) and the fare breakdown (EV-FARE-00102) all carry the identical trip_id TRP-00102, and the trace opens at 2026-07-19T11:23:30, the exact started_at recorded on the trip record. There is no trip-identity dispute for the driver to exploit.

The driver's own message concedes the detour. Sent at 11:29:04 and read by the rider at 11:29:40, it reads 'boss BKE quite jam, i go Upper Bukit Timah ok?' — an admission in the chat_log that the vehicle left the booked corridor, and an independent source of exactly the kind POL-RD-07(ii) recognises. It also shuts the driver out of POL-RD-04: the instruction came from the DRIVER, not the rider, and chat_message.waypoint_hint is null, so there is no rider-requested detour on this record and no corroboration of one; under POL-RD-08 the driver must point to a specific artifact and clause, and this one cannot be run.

The driver's explanation — a BKE crawl near Dairy Farm, per his counterparty statement — is asserted with no evidence ID and is tested against this trip's traffic advisory and nothing else. EV-ADVIS-00102-01 is MISSING: admissibility status MISSING, weight_multiplier 0.0, issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT, with no LTA advisory covering the BKE or the Upper Bukit Timah corridor in the 11:16–11:55 window. The rider relies on the absence itself, which POL-GEN-02 makes citable, and not on any payload. Because no advisory exists, the POL-RD-03 comparison cannot be run, the assertion carries no weight under POL-RD-08, and the driver is left with no exoneration at all.

The driver tells the platform he 'did not charge anything extra', and the fare breakdown contradicts him. total_charged is SGD 29.91, while the same trip recomputed on the booked optimal route — (3.80 + 0.75 x 20.4 + 0.28 x 27) x surge multiplier 1.0 read from the fare breakdown, plus the 0.80 platform fee, with no ERP, no tolls and no promo — is SGD 27.46. The rider therefore paid SGD 2.45 more than the optimal route supports, and the driver's denial of an extra charge cannot be credited against the ledger.

The rider does not overstate the arithmetic. On the figure POL-RD-01 makes governing — gps_trace.trace_distance_km, 21.79 km, not the rounded 21.8 km convenience copy on the trip record — the excess over the 20.4 km booked optimal is 1.39 km, or 6.81%. Both POL-RD-01 establishment tests must pass and the percentage test does not: 6.81% sits below the 20% gate (4.08 km for this optimal). No deviation is therefore established and POL-RD-02 cannot be run, so the rider's monetary claim cannot be carried on this evidence. The rider notes the consequence under POL-GEN-03 rather than hiding it: with payment_status CHARGED and refund_issued_sgd 0.0, a no-action outcome leaves the rider bearing the whole charge. The point is conceded, not stretched.

ruling.explanation:
Both parties' arithmetic, and the record, agree on the governing measurement. The GPS trace EV-GPS-00102 (weight 1.0) records trace_distance_km 21.79 against the booked optimal of 20.4 km on EV-TRIP-00102, an excess of 1.39 km — 6.81% of optimal. POL-RD-01 establishes a route deviation only when the excess is greater than 20% of optimal AND greater than 0.8 km absolute, and both limbs must pass. The absolute limb is met (1.39 km > 0.8 km) but the percentage limb is not (6.81% against 20%, i.e. 4.08 km for this optimal). No deviation is established, and POL-RD-01 fixes the outcome at NO_ACTION however the rider characterises the trip. The trace figure governs, not the rounded 21.8 km convenience copy on the trip record, but either figure gives the same result. The trace is unimpaired: 100% coverage, 193 fixes, no gaps, 10 s sampling, so POL-RD-07 and POL-RD-10(3) are not engaged.

On the rider's points: (1) The driver's chat message EV-CHAT-00102 — 'boss BKE quite jam, i go Upper Bukit Timah ok?' at 11:29:04, read 11:29:40 — is accepted as showing the vehicle left the BKE corridor, and the driver's counterparty statement accepts the same. But POL-RD-01's establishment test is numeric, and an admitted corridor change does not substitute for an excess clearing 20%; the same evidence confirms the change was small ('same distance more or less'; 1.39 km on the trace). (2) The fare differential is accepted as arithmetic but is not payable: charged_total 29.91 less the platform's recomputed optimal fare 27.46 is 2.45, but POL-RD-02 runs only on a deviation first established under POL-RD-01, and none is. The 29.91 is the metered fare correctly built from base 3.80 + distance 16.35 + time 8.96 + platform fee 0.80 for the distance and time actually driven. (3) POL-RD-09(4) gives nothing: erp_gantries is empty, tolls_erp 0.00 and airport_surcharge 0.00, so there is no phantom gantry line or misapplied surcharge to correct, and that is the only route to money on a no-deviation finding.

On the driver's points: the assertion of a BKE crawl near Dairy Farm is an external-traffic assertion. The only traffic advisory for this trip, EV-ADVIS-00102-01, is MISSING — status MISSING, weight_multiplier 0.0, issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT — and no LTA advisory covers the BKE or the Upper Bukit Timah corridor in the 11:16–11:55 window. Under POL-RD-13 and POL-RD-08 the comparison cannot be run, POL-RD-03 is unavailable, and the assertion carries no weight; it neither reduces the excess nor supplies an amended optimal. The driver cites no advisory identifier for the excuse, so the absence is a gap in the bundle and not a POL-RD-10(5) escalation. The point is in any event immaterial: with no deviation established there is nothing to exculpate.

POL-RD-04 is unavailable: the corridor instruction came from the DRIVER, not the rider, the rider never replied, and chat_message.waypoint_hint is null, so there is no rider-requested detour to corroborate. POL-RD-06 is not engaged — no material deviation, and driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d is 0 of 640 completed trips — so no conduct referral fires. POL-RD-11 does not apply (fare_model METERED, not UPFRONT_QUOTE) and POL-RD-12 does not apply (vehicle_type RYDE_PLUS, not RYDE_POOL). No billing-integrity referral under POL-RD-09(4) and no false-arrival referral arise.

Confidence: the deciding fact — the excess measurement — is carried by EV-GPS-00102 and EV-TRIP-00102, both at weight_multiplier 1.0, so the POL-GEN-02(2) cap is 1.0. The MISSING advisory at weight 0.0 carries no fact and does not cap anything. No POL-RD-10 trigger fires: identifiers all match TRP-00102, timestamps agree, no cited artifact is missing in support of an invoked exculpatory clause, and no refund exceeds the ceiling.

Outcome: the rider's claim is not supported on this record. payment_status CHARGED and refund_issued_sgd 0.00 stand as they are; the disputed 29.91 is neither refunded nor held, and no money moves to either party.

This is decided on the distance arithmetic both sides agree about. The booked optimal route for TRP-00102 is 20.4 km (trip record). The governing measurement of the distance actually driven is the GPS trace — gps_trace.trace_distance_km = 21.79 km, not the rounded 21.8 km copy on the trip record, as POL-RD-01 requires. The excess is therefore 1.39 km, which is 6.81% of optimal. POL-RD-01 establishes a deviation only where the excess exceeds BOTH 20% of optimal AND 0.8 km; both limbs must pass. The absolute limb is met (1.39 km), the percentage limb is not (6.81% against 20%, i.e. a 4.08 km gate), and so no route deviation is established. Under POL-RD-01 the outcome is NO_ACTION however the trip is characterised.

That holds even though the driver's own chat message at 11:29 ('boss BKE quite jam, i go Upper Bukit Timah ok?', read by the rider at 11:29:40) concedes he left the booked corridor. An admission can establish that a different road was taken, but POL-RD-01 measures a deviation by distance excess, and this trip's excess does not clear the gate. The message is also not a rider instruction, so POL-RD-04 (rider-requested detour) is unavailable to the driver; that makes no difference, because no deviation exists to exonerate. The driver's separate account of a BKE crawl near Dairy Farm is an external-traffic assertion, and under POL-RD-13 and POL-RD-08 it is tested against this trip's traffic advisory and nothing else. EV-ADVIS-00102-01 is MISSING (weight_multiplier 0.0, issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT) — no LTA advisory covers the BKE or Upper Bukit Timah corridor in the 11:16–11:55 window — so the POL-RD-03 comparison cannot be run and the assertion carries no weight. It does not escalate the case: the driver cited no advisory identifier, and POL-RD-13(1) provides that an assertion citing no artifact cannot be invoked against one.

The rider's arithmetic is sound but premature. Recomputing the fare on the booked optimal route — (3.80 + 0.75 × 20.4 + 0.28 × 27) × 1.0 surge multiplier read from the fare breakdown, + 0.80 platform fee, no ERP, no tolls, no promo — gives SGD 27.46 against the SGD 29.91 charged, a differential of SGD 2.45. The driver's statement that he 'did not charge anything extra' is contradicted by the ledger, but that differential is payable only under POL-RD-02, which runs only once a deviation is established under POL-RD-01. None is, so the SGD 2.45 is not refundable. There is no standalone correction either: under POL-RD-09(4) the fare breakdown carries no ERP gantries (tolls_erp 0.00, erp_gantries empty) and no airport surcharge (0.00), so there is no phantom line to refund.

Under POL-GEN-03, NO_ACTION is party-relative: fare_breakdown.payment_status is CHARGED and refund_issued_sgd is 0.00, so on this rider-filed dispute the charge stands exactly as it is — nothing is collected and nothing is refunded. The rider's profile counters (deviation_claims_60d = 2, deviation_claims_60d_substantiated = 0) fall below the POL-RD-08 thresholds and impose no extra corroboration; no other profile field bears on the outcome (POL-GEN-01). The threshold finding rests on the GPS trace and the trip record, both at weight 1.0, and no deciding artifact is impaired. No clause in this category produces a referral on these facts.

ruling.explanation:
This ruling is addressed to both parties. Both sides ultimately agree on the decisive arithmetic, and so does the tribunal.

THE DISTANCE TEST (POL-RD-01). The governing measure of the distance actually driven is the GPS trace figure, gps_trace.trace_distance_km = 21.79 km (EV-GPS-00102), not the rounded 21.8 km convenience copy on the trip record (EV-TRIP-00102); POL-RD-01 makes the trace figure govern for the threshold test. The booked optimal distance is 20.4 km (EV-TRIP-00102). The excess is therefore 1.39 km, which is 6.81% of optimal. POL-RD-01 establishes a route deviation only when the excess passes BOTH limbs — more than 20% of optimal AND more than 0.8 km absolute. The absolute limb passes (1.39 km > 0.8 km), but the percentage limb does not (6.81% is below 20%, i.e. below the 4.08 km that the 20% gate implies for a 20.4 km route). Both limbs must pass, so no route deviation is established on this trip, and POL-RD-01 fixes the outcome at NO_ACTION however the trip is characterised.

THE MONEY. POL-RD-02 (optimal-route fare recomputation) runs only where a deviation is first established under POL-RD-01. It is not, so the SGD 2.45 differential between charged_total (SGD 29.91) and the recomputed optimal-route fare (SGD 27.46, per EV-FARE-00102) is not payable and no partial refund issues. To the rider's point that the driver told the platform he 'did not charge anything extra' while the ledger shows SGD 2.45 more than the optimal route supports: that arithmetic observation is correct, and the driver's denial is not credited against the ledger. But it does not open a refund route POL-RD-01 has closed — the charge is refundable only if a deviation is established or a billing-integrity defect exists, and neither is present.

BILLING INTEGRITY (POL-RD-09(4)). Checked and clean. The fare breakdown carries no ERP gantries (erp_gantries empty, tolls_erp SGD 0.00, off-optimal-route ERP total SGD 0.00) and no airport surcharge (airport_surcharge SGD 0.00), so there is no phantom charge line to refund as a standalone correction.

THE DRIVER'S TRAFFIC EXCUSE (POL-RD-13, POL-RD-03, POL-RD-08). The driver's explanation for the route — a BKE crawl near Dairy Farm — is an external-traffic assertion, and POL-RD-13 tests it against this trip's traffic advisory and nothing else. The only advisory in the bundle, EV-ADVIS-00102-01, is MISSING (weight_multiplier 0.0, issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT): no LTA advisory covers the BKE or the Upper Bukit Timah corridor in the 11:16–11:55 window. The POL-RD-03 comparison therefore cannot be run, and the assertion carries no weight under POL-RD-08 and POL-RD-13. I record that the assertion is discarded and that no advisory was on file. It is immaterial in any event: because the rider's excess never clears the POL-RD-01 threshold, the case is decided on the threshold, not on the driver's excuse. The driver cited no advisory identifier, so the missing advisory is not an exculpatory clause invoked against a cited artifact and POL-RD-10(5) is not engaged; the trace is also unimpaired (100% coverage, no gaps, 10 s sampling), so POL-RD-07 and POL-RD-10(3) do not fire either.

THE CHAT MESSAGE (POL-RD-04). The driver's message at 11:29:04 ('boss BKE quite jam, i go Upper Bukit Timah ok?', EV-CHAT-00102) is accepted as a driver statement. Both sides are right that it leaves POL-RD-04 unavailable: the only recorded instruction came from the driver, not the rider, and chat_message.waypoint_hint is null, so there is no rider-requested detour to exonerate or to exclude. The point does not change the outcome, because there is no established deviation to exonerate or to refund. No driver-conduct pattern is present (driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d = 0 against 214 completed trips in 30 days), no material deviation exists, and no billing-integrity or false-arrival referral arises — hence the referrals list is empty.

OUTCOME. Under POL-GEN-03, NO_ACTION is party-relative and leaves the present state standing. The fare breakdown records payment_status CHARGED and refund_issued_sgd 0.00, so on this rider-filed dispute the charge of SGD 29.91 stands exactly as it is and no money moves to either party. Confidence is set at 0.92; the deciding facts (trace_distance_km and optimal_distance_km) are carried by artifacts at weight 1.0 (EV-GPS-00102, EV-TRIP-00102), so nothing caps the ruling below the 0.70 floor.

ruling.explanation:
To the rider and the driver: the disputed charge of SGD 29.91 stands and no money moves. Here is why.

POL-RD-01 establishes a route deviation only if the driven distance exceeds the booked optimal by BOTH more than 0.8 km and more than 20% of optimal. The governing measurement is the GPS trace (EV-GPS-00102, weight 1.0): 21.79 km. The booked optimal route (EV-TRIP-00102, weight 1.0) is 20.4 km. The excess is 1.39 km — over the 0.8 km limb, but only 6.81% of optimal, far under the 20% limb. Both limbs must pass, so no deviation is established on this trip. The trip record's rounded 21.8 km copy makes no difference and may not be cited for the test.

The driver did leave the BKE corridor: his own message in the chat log (EV-CHAT-00102, weight 1.0), sent at 11:29:04, reads 'boss BKE quite jam, i go Upper Bukit Timah ok?' That is an admission against his own interest and it is accepted as showing the corridor was left. But POL-RD-01's numeric gate is what decides whether a deviation exists, and the detour cost only 1.39 km (6.81%). The driver's account of a BKE crawl near Dairy Farm is asserted with no LTA advisory on file — EV-ADVIS-00102-01 is MISSING, weight_multiplier 0.0, issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT. Under POL-RD-13 that assertion carries no weight and supplies no amended optimal, but it does not change the result and the driver does not need it, because the threshold already fails. Because the driver cited no advisory identifier, the missing advisory is a gap in the bundle and not an exculpatory clause invoked against a cited artifact, so POL-RD-10(5) is not engaged and this does not escalate. POL-RD-04 is not relied on by either side: the chat message is the driver's, not a rider instruction, and waypoint_hint is null, so no rider-requested detour could be run.

The fare differential the rider points to — charged_total SGD 29.91 against a recomputed optimal-route fare of SGD 27.46, i.e. SGD 2.45 (both from EV-FARE-00102) — is not payable. POL-RD-02 runs only after a deviation is first established under POL-RD-01, and none is. Neither is there any standalone correction under POL-RD-09(4): the fare carries no ERP gantries (erp_gantries empty, tolls_erp 0.00) and no airport surcharge (0.00), so no phantom line exists to refund.

Because the establishment test fails, POL-RD-01 fixes the outcome at NO_ACTION however the rider characterises the trip. Under POL-GEN-03 that is party-relative and leaves the payment state as it is: the fare_breakdown records payment_status CHARGED and refund_issued_sgd 0.00, so the SGD 29.91 charge stands. No driver-conduct referral arises: the driver's deviation_flags_90d is 0 and the deviation here is not material, so POL-RD-06 is not engaged. Confidence is 0.90, resting on the weight-1.0 GPS trace and trip record that carry the deciding measurement.
